name: Dev Resources

sources.title: Dev Resources homepage — collaborative list of 800+ developer resources
CONTRIBUTING.md — resource format and eligibility rules

requirements: Only resources 'highly or exclusively related to programming and development' are accepted
No duplicates — search the README first
Contribution happens via pull request on marcelscruz/dev-resources (the site also shows a 'Submit' link and sign-in, but the canonical documented path is the repo)
Resource format: name (required), description (required), up to 3 categories (required), url (required), optional keywords
preparation: Resource name, URL (must start with http(s)), description (metatags.io suggested for pulling it), category picks (max 3), optional keywords
Check the README/­/resources folder that the resource isn't already listed
workflow: Locate the alphabetically correct file in /resources based on the resource's name property
Add a resource object (name, description, categories, url, keywords) preserving alphabetical order
Open a PR against main and complete the PR template checklist
Maintainer review merges; the site regenerates (README and /db are auto-generated — do not edit them)
watchFor: README.md and /db are auto-generated — editing them is explicitly banned and wastes the PR
Marketing-flavored or tangential products are out of scope — dev-tooling relevance is the gate
Site 'Submit' button exists but the documented, authoritative path is the GitHub PR
If TypeScript is a barrier, CONTRIBUTING says to open an issue with the resource's info instead
countsAsLive: The resource card appears in a category listing on devresourc.es and in the repo's generated README
unknowns: Whether the on-site Submit form (behind sign-in) is equivalent to the PR route
Whether outbound links are dofollow (favicon-list style entries)
